pack.title: One uppers
pack.description: Ask to be heard before switching stories.

scenarios.setting: You tell a friend about your difficult week and they immediately compare it to theirs.
scenarios.jab: That's nothing; you should hear what happened to me.
scenarios.goal: Ask to be heard before switching stories.

replies.line: I want to hear yours. Let me finish mine first.
replies.why: It makes room for both stories while protecting your turn.
replies.delivery: Emphasize “finish mine first,” then continue your story rather than adding a second request.

replies.why: It requests the immediate behavior you need without debating whose week was worse.
replies.delivery: Say “Let me finish this first” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” then continue your story rather than adding a second request.

replies.line: That sounds hard too; could you hear me out before we switch?
replies.why: It recognizes their experience while asking for attention to yours.
replies.delivery: Keep “That sounds hard too” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. ” then continue your story rather than adding a second request.

replies.line: One disaster at a time; mine's still on stage.
replies.why: Humor interrupts the comparison without making suffering into a competition.
replies.delivery: Keep “One disaster at a time” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” then continue your story rather than adding a second request.

followUp.jab: I'm just saying I get it.
followUp.line: I appreciate that; listening for a minute would help me more right now.
followUp.why: It specifies the support you need instead of arguing about their intention.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “I appreciate that,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
